content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a complete responsive bookmark manager called **Stash**.

Included:

- Add and delete bookmarks
- Search across titles, URLs, descriptions, and tags
- Collections and favorites
- Grid and list layouts
- Copy and open-link actions
- Persistent browser storage
- Responsive mobile navigation
- Polished empty states and notifications

Validation passed:

- Production build succeeds
- Desktop bookmark workflow tested
- Mobile navigation tested
- 2/2 Playwright tests passing

The app is ready at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This looks really nice — clean, and I can see my saved links, search them, favorite them, and sort them. Two things stop it from actually doing what I need, though:

1. **Saving a link is too much manual work.** When I click "Add bookmark" it makes me type in the title and description myself. What I really want is to just paste a link and have the app pull in the page's name (and ideally a short description/icon) automatically — that's the whole point of "saving" a bookmark for me. Right now it won't even save unless I hand-type a title.

2. **I can't fix a bookmark after saving it.** I can add one and delete one, but there's no way to go back and edit a saved link — change its title, its tags, or move it. Part of managing my bookmarks is tidying them up after the fact.

Everything else here is a good start. Could you get those two working — the automatic pulling-in of the page info when I paste a link, and being able to edit an existing bookmark?

content:
Implemented both requested improvements.

- Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its page title, description, and favicon.
- Title is no longer required—the domain becomes a fallback if metadata cannot be retrieved.
- Added a manual “Fetch details” retry button.
- Added an Edit action to each bookmark’s overflow menu.
- Editing supports the URL, title, description, collection, and tags.
- Metadata fetching includes redirect limits and private-network protection.

Verified with browser tests covering automatic metadata retrieval, saving, editing, tags, and mobile navigation. All tests pass.

Updated app: [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000)

That's exactly what I was after. I pasted-in behavior aside, I can see it pulls the page's real title and description automatically now, and there's a proper Edit option on each bookmark that lets me change the link, title, tags, and where it lives. Both of those do the job for me — approved.
